title: Rethinking the role of animal models in adaptive deep brain stimulation: From feasibility to mechanistic and disease-modifying insights
title_zh: 重新思考动物模型在自适应深脑刺激中的作用：从可行性到机制与疾病修饰洞察
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS) has emerged as an advanced neuromodulation approach capable of dynamically adjusting stimulation parameters based on real-time biomarkers, thereby overcoming the limitations of conventional continuous DBS (cDBS). While early animal studies were instrumental in establishing the feasibility and symptomatic efficacy of aDBS, its availability in humans poses the question of whether animal studies are still needed in this field. OBJECTIVE: This review aims to critically reassess the role of animal models in the development and future evolution of aDBS, with particular emphasis on their contribution to mechanistic insights, potential disease-modifying effects, biomarker identification, and the integration of machine learning for next-generation adaptive neuromodulation systems. FINDINGS: Animal studies have provided the foundational evidence for closed-loop neuromodulation, demonstrating the feasibility of real-time sensing-stimulation systems and the initial superiority of aDBS over cDBS in modulating motor symptoms. Preclinical models have enabled the identification and causal validation of electrophysiological and neurochemical biomarkers while also serving as indispensable platforms for hardware innovation, causal circuit interrogation using optogenetics, and validation of machine learning-based adaptive control algorithms. Moreover, animal models offer a unique platform for investigating disease progression, neural plasticity, and stage-dependent effects of stimulation, which remain difficult to assess in human studies. In parallel, machine learning approaches have increasingly leveraged preclinical and clinical data to decode physiological states, optimize stimulation parameters, and dynamically adapt therapy, thus supporting the development of personalized aDBS systems. CONCLUSION: The role of animal models in aDBS research is undergoing a conceptual transition, from demonstrating feasibility and symptomatic efficacy to addressing mechanistic and disease-modifying questions. By enabling causal investigation of neural circuits, hardware development, biomarker validation, and integration with machine learning frameworks, preclinical research remains essential for advancing aDBS toward more precise, adaptive, and potentially disease-modifying neuromodulation strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景：自适应深脑刺激（aDBS）已成为一种先进的神经调制方法，能够根据实时生物标志物动态调整刺激参数，从而克服传统连续深脑刺激（cDBS）的局限。早期动物研究在确立aDBS的可行性和症状缓解效果方面起到了关键作用，但在人类中的应用使人们质疑该领域是否仍需要动物研究。目的：本综述旨在批判性重新评估动物模型在aDBS开发和未来演进中的作用，特别强调其在机制洞察、潜在疾病修饰效应、生物标志物识别以及将机器学习整合到下一代自适应神经调制系统中的贡献。发现：动物研究为闭环神经调制提供了基础证据，证明了实时感知-刺激系统的可行性，并初步显示aDBS在调节运动症状方面优于cDBS。临床前模型使得电生理和神经化学生物标志物的识别与因果验证成为可能，同时也是硬件创新、光遗传学因果电路探测以及基于机器学习的自适应控制算法验证的不可或缺的平台。此外，动物模型为研究疾病进展、神经可塑性和刺激的阶段依赖效应提供了独特平台，这在人体研究中仍难以评估。与此同时，机器学习方法越来越多地利用临床前和临床数据来解码生理状态、优化刺激参数并动态适应治疗，从而支持个性化aDBS系统的发展。结论：动物模型在aDBS研究中的角色正经历概念转变，从证明可行性和症状缓解转向解决机制与疾病修饰问题。通过实现神经回路的因果研究、硬件开发、生物标志物验证以及与机器学习框架的整合，临床前研究仍然是推动aDBS迈向更精准、自适应且潜在疾病修饰神经调制策略的关键。
